transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I guess the main reason I came in today is, well, it's probably nothing major, but I've just been getting pulled off track kind of easily? 

Like, I'll be working on something—recently I was supposed to be finishing up this dashboard for a project—and it just takes one little thing to derail me. A Slack ping will pop up, or I'll catch a song lyric in the background, or I'll even just get a random idea for a totally different project. And suddenly I realize I've completely lost the thread of what I was actually supposed to be doing. 

I mean, I know everyone gets distracted sometimes, so I might just need to try harder to focus. I don't want to make a big deal out of nothing. But it's been bothering me a little bit. Does... does that make sense? Is that the right kind of thing to bring up here?
Before this recent work situation, did you have similar attention or distractibility problems when you were a child?

Um, yeah, I guess so? I really don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or a troublemaker or anything, because I really did try to be good! But... yeah, I suppose it's been going on for a while. 

Even back in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes write little comments on my report cards about me rushing through my worksheets, or kind of losing track of the directions. And, um, I guess I had a bad habit of talking over my classmates during group work? I think I was just really eager to share, but I know it probably wasn't great. 

And at home, my parents actually used to sit right beside me while I did my homework. Because if they didn't, I would just kind of wander off, or I'd start doing something totally different before I even finished the assignment. 

I hope that doesn't sound too terrible? I know a lot of kids need help staying on task with homework, so maybe it was just normal kid stuff... is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
Did these attention and distractibility problems start before you were 12 years old?

Oh! Um, yes. I'm sorry, I probably should have just given you an exact age a second ago so I didn't make you ask twice! 

But yes, definitely before I was twelve. Like I was just saying about elementary school... when my teachers were writing those notes about me rushing through my worksheets and losing track of the directions, and when my parents had to sit with me so I wouldn't wander off from my homework... I was probably only seven or eight years old then? 

So yeah, it was definitely before twelve. I'm really sorry to repeat myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline. Is that... is that the kind of answer you needed?
Do these attention problems cause you trouble in more than one part of your life, like at work and at home?

Um, yeah, I guess it does pop up in a few different places. I really don't want it to sound like my life is falling apart or anything, because it's definitely not! I'm doing okay. But... well, I guess it does affect a couple of things. 

Like, with my career stuff—I'm not working full-time right now, I'm just doing freelance design and trying to build my portfolio while I finish my degree. And, um, I have lost a couple of small freelance contracts recently. And there was this portfolio competition I really wanted to enter, but I missed the deadline. I think people just feel like they can't totally rely on me to follow through cleanly on the details, even if they really like my initial ideas. 

And, um, it's kind of spilled over into my personal life, too. A few of my friends have seemed a little... hesitant to collaborate with me on projects lately. Which I completely understand! I know it's frustrating when someone gets distracted. I just feel bad that I'm letting them down. 

I'm trying really hard to get better at it, though! I don't want to be a burden on anyone. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm not complaining too much.
Do you also have these attention problems outside of work or school, like at home or in other everyday activities?

Um, well, yes... a little bit, I guess. I mean, I really try to stay organized with my everyday stuff, I promise I do! I have all these systems set up. But, um... I guess I do still forget some basic things sometimes. 

Like, if a freelance client leaves a message, or if I need to send a quick follow-up email, it sometimes just... slips my mind. Or even just normal things, like remembering to bring my sketchbook to a meetup with friends. I actually have to set multiple alarms and reminders on my phone for everything. And, honestly... sometimes I just swipe the notification away because I'm in the middle of something else, and then I completely forget about it again. 

I know that sounds really irresponsible, and I feel so terrible when it happens! I'm really working on being better about it. I hope it doesn't make me sound like a complete mess... is that the kind of everyday stuff you were asking about?
Do your concentration problems get noticeably worse during periods of stress?

Um, stress? I don't... I don't think so? I mean, I try really hard not to let things get to me, so I wouldn't say stress makes it worse. 

If anything, when I'm stressed, I think I almost try harder to focus? Like, I know I need to get things done, so I really push myself. I'm not always perfect at it, obviously, but I don't think it's a huge issue. 

I mean, everyone gets a little scattered when they're overwhelmed, right? I don't think I'm any worse than a normal person when things get busy. I hope that's a good thing? Like, it means I can handle pressure okay, right?
Have you been having a low or depressed mood most days lately?

Um, depressed? No, no, definitely not! I mean, I have my moments where I get a little frustrated with myself, like when I mess up a project or forget something important, but I really try to stay positive! 

I honestly feel pretty lucky most of the time. I get to study design and do things I enjoy. I'm definitely not walking around feeling sad or low every day. I try to keep a smile on my face and not let things drag me down, you know? 

I hope that's what you were looking for? I really don't want you to think I'm unhappy or anything, because I'm honestly doing fine in that department!
Do you often feel restless or find yourself fidgeting or unable to sit still?

Um, well... I guess I do move around a bit? But I really don't think it's that bad! I mean, I try so hard to sit still, especially when it's important. 

But, um... sometimes, like during portfolio reviews or longer meetings, I guess I do catch myself... doing things? Like, I might be bouncing my leg a little, or maybe clicking my pen, or twisting my rings around. And I honestly don't even realize I'm doing it until, you know, someone glances over at me. Then I stop immediately, I promise! I just get a little nervous, maybe? Or I'm just trying to stay focused on what they're saying. 

I really try not to be disruptive or anything. I just... shift around in my chair sometimes. That's pretty normal for someone my age, right? Like, a lot of people fidget a little bit when they have to sit for a long time? I hope it doesn't make me seem disrespectful or anything when I do it...

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation, with symptoms beginning in childhood, present across multiple settings, and causing functional impairment. The patient confirmed longstanding distractibility, losing track of tasks, forgetfulness, disorganization, and some mild hyperactive/fidgety behaviors. Symptoms were clearly present before age 12 and have affected work, school, and daily activities. F98.8 was considered, but the developmental onset and pervasive pattern favor ADHD rather than an unspecified attention disorder.
